source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Land preparation for corn requires two rounds of plowing/tilling, timed relative to planting:

First tillage (ភ្លូវលើកទី១): should be plowed within a window of about 15 to 50 days before the planting date. This tillage should be done to a depth of about 15 to 25 cm. Tilling should turn over about 30 to 50% of the soil so it can be exposed to sunlight and weathering. If tillage is done during dry conditions (before the rains, timed to the seasonal calendar), after the first tillage the soil should be left to weather/dry out and to allow water to evaporate from within the soil.

Second tillage (ភ្លូវលើកទី២): the second tillage is done about 1 to 3 days before planting, i.e. shortly before the corn is sown. This second tillage is specifically for smoothing/breaking down large clods, particularly at the point when soil moisture is appropriate for planting -- the aim is to prepare the soil bed so it is loose and workable for good germination.

The second tillage should be plowed to a depth of about 20 to 25 cm, and this tillage should be done with an implement suitable for creating a fine planting bed.
